To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) psychiatry residents who complete a 6-month addiction psychiatry elective are more likely to treat substance abuse patients and are less likely to be stigmatizing of these patients than residents who do not complete an addiction elective; and (b) residents who complete an addiction elective are more likely than residents who do an addiction rotation to treat substance abuse disorders, and are equally likely to treat substance abusers with co-occurring disorders.
